title: Finite common-word OS versus direct D/delta-D route bridge
question: Does the finite OS common-word context decay seen in EXP-001174/001175 align with the direct D/delta-D route, or do the finite OS deltas decrease while direct seminorm maxima grow with volume?

adversarial_review.check: The bridge reads only committed EXP-001149, EXP-001169 and EXP-001175 run JSONs and records their paths; it does not recompute or silently alter upstream values.
OS Gram context deltas and direct D/delta-D maxima are different finite diagnostics; ratios are reported descriptively and are not treated as a common norm.
Only matching declared volume labels are compared; path4/path5/path6 and source-weight volumes 2/4/6 are not conflated as one exhaustion theorem.
Finite increase/decrease predicates are computed from the full recorded sequences and are not promoted to asymptotic bounds.
D and delta-D maxima retain their source, beta, cutoff and finite fixture boundaries; growth is not called an impossibility theorem for every weighted norm.
The independent bridge consumes only the independent upstream runs and reproduces all derived bridge fields independently of the primary lane.
Lean R247 is rerun as an exact finite Gibbs/scope crosscheck; bridge arithmetic remains a transparent Python audit of committed JSON inputs.
Mixed finite-route behavior does not prove or refute a thermodynamic OS state, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R247 verifies the exact finite Gibbs and conditional-transfer boundary; the bridge does not claim Lean formalization of dense Q3 outputs.

qft_interface.closed: The finite OS context deltas, direct D/delta-D volume maxima and source-weighted direct maxima are provenance-linked, independently reproduced and compared as route diagnostics.
qft_interface.open: An analytic estimate connecting the OS word norm to a source/volume/cutoff/beta-uniform direct seminorm remains open, as do common-word exhaustion embedding, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 route-selection evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the mixed signal to seek an analytic inequality with explicit source-distance and direct-seminorm weights; do not infer that finite OS decay repairs the unclosed direct D/delta-D Cauchy gate.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite route bridge. It is not a theorem identifying any finite diagnostic with a thermodynamic QFT norm or state.
no_overclaim: This package only re-aggregates committed finite diagnostics. It does not prove a common OS carrier, direct Cauchy convergence, common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS identification, a mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
